cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the surrender is happening as it should.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Tend something you're steering — hands on it, unhurried, watching what it needs today. Feel where to push and where to leave it be. Let what it does next tell you.
cells.core:
You can hold a goal and let go of pushing at the same time. The momentum stays, and there's no strain in it. Anyone watching feels the difference: something moves because you're carrying it, not because you're forcing it. That's not softness. It's the sure grip, the one that knows it can open its hand.
Tend a piece of what you're steering this week. Not the plan for it, the thing itself — hands on it, unhurried, seeing what it needs today. Watch where it grows without your push and where it actually does need you. That's the same read you want on the bigger goals: which motion is yours to drive and which belongs to the thing's own timing.
cells.sheetLine: The sure grip is the one that can open.

cells.tense: You are standing where the goal is already decided and the work is not started.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Set the facts of a goal down in order on paper, no feeling words in the list. Follow the last fact to the next real step. If the writing points elsewhere than your plan, take that seriously.
cells.core:
You are already living on the far side of where this was decided. The momentum runs past the work, so today's motions feel like delays and every hour gets spent bracing for an outcome you can't make arrive sooner. Pushing harder doesn't make the future come in faster. It just puts your weight where nothing can hold it yet.
Slow that down with facts. Write what's actually true about the goal right now — what you've done, what's finished, what hasn't moved. No feelings in the list; feelings lie about timing. What's on paper is what you can act on. Follow the last true fact to the next real step and do that one. The push lands where it can move something.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Lay the single step toward a goal you can already see — do it fully, edge to edge. Nothing past it. Rest when it's down.
cells.core:
The direction is still in you, but the energy that used to carry it isn't reaching today. Something got put down, and now even wanting to move feels heavy. You're looking back at what's behind the door. The momentum hasn't gone; it's parked.
Don't try to want it back. Find the one step toward a goal you can see without guessing, and lay it today. Do it fully, the way a builder sets a stone so the next one has somewhere to sit. That single step, edge to edge. The direction returns through the ground you stand on, not through the feeling of wanting to move.

cells.tense: You are still writing, and no one has credited you for the hand you are.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Go at something you run with clean hands — no plan, just look at what it actually needs and give it that. Watch what it asks for, and keep what you learn.
cells.core:
You keep a lot moving, and you have a name for how: disciplined, steady, hard-working. Those are the habits. Underneath them is a real read for what a thing needs and when to hold it or release it. That's the part that's yours, and it's the part you don't say.
Use it with clean hands. Take something you run and look at it like you just inherited it — fresh eyes, no plan, see what it actually needs and give it that. Watch what asks to move and what asks to rest. That's your read being used. If it turns out you were the one choosing, keep the knowledge. It shouldn't stay in the drawer.
cells.sheetLine: You were the one shaping this, not just following it.
